categories.main_business_segments: KATITAS Co., Ltd. operates primarily in the 'pre-owned home revitalization business,' which involves purchasing, renovating, and reselling used detached houses. The group consists of the parent company and one consolidated subsidiary (Reprice), both engaged in this single business segment. Other business activities, such as rental or brokerage, are not material to segment reporting.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company’s core operational method is a vertically integrated process: it acquires used homes (mainly through direct purchase), inspects and evaluates them with a proprietary checklist (including joint inspections with renovation partners and termite inspectors), and then renovates them to modern standards. Renovations are standardized and cost-optimized through bulk procurement and long-term partnerships with local contractors, ensuring consistent quality and efficient turnaround.
categories.primary_customers_markets: KATITAS primarily serves individual homebuyers, especially families and first-time buyers seeking affordable, high-quality housing alternatives to new builds or rentals. The company’s main markets are regional cities and suburban areas across Japan, with a focus on areas where new housing supply is limited and demand for affordable, renovated homes is strong.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates nationwide in Japan, with 149 locations as of March 2025. Its core focus is on regional cities with populations between 50,000 and 300,000 for KATITAS, and suburban areas of major metropolitan regions (Tokyo, Nagoya, Osaka) and regional city centers for Reprice. All assets and sales are domestic.
categories.supply_chain_position: KATITAS is positioned downstream in the real estate supply chain, acting as both acquirer and end-seller of residential properties. It sources properties directly from individuals or via auctions, renovates them, and sells directly to end-users or through real estate agents.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding sales staff and training, improving productivity through digitalization and process optimization, diversifying renovation offerings to meet changing customer needs, and broadening sourcing channels (including partnerships with local governments and other industries). Sustainability is emphasized, with initiatives to reduce CO2 emissions and promote the reuse of vacant homes. M&A is considered for further growth, and the company aims for stable, not rapid, expansion.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is generated primarily through the sale of renovated pre-owned homes. The company purchases properties, invests in renovations, and sells them at a margin. Sales are made both directly to consumers (via company and third-party websites) and through real estate agents. There is no recurring revenue model; income is transaction-based.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: KATITAS is the market leader in Japan’s pre-owned home revitalization sector, especially in regional and older detached housing markets where entry barriers are high due to property risks and local knowledge requirements. While large homebuilders and real estate companies have entered the market, most have withdrawn due to the complexity and risk. In suburban and urban areas, competition is more intense, but KATITAS maintains an edge through scale, speed, and proprietary know-how.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending March 2025, consolidated sales reached 129.5 billion yen, with operating profit of 14.2 billion yen and net profit attributable to shareholders of 9.6 billion yen. The company has shown steady growth in sales and profits over recent years, with a 2.2% increase in sales and 12.4% increase in net profit year-on-year. Total assets are 83.3 billion yen, and the company employs 922 people. The growth trajectory is stable, with a focus on sustainable expansion.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: KATITAS offers a unique value proposition by providing 'the fourth option' in housing: affordable, high-quality, fully renovated pre-owned homes that are neither new, as-is used, nor rental. The company differentiates itself through its nationwide network, deep local knowledge, standardized renovation quality, and ability to supply homes at about half the price of new builds. Its early entry and accumulated know-how in challenging regional markets create significant competitive barriers.
